L240: The functional $\en_{\omega}$ is increasing and satisfies $\en_{\omega}(\varphi+c)=\en_{\omega}(\varphi)+c$ for any $\varphi\in\PSH(\omega)$ and $c\in\mathbb{R}$. We have $(\omega_{0},\varphi_{0})\cdot\ldots\cdot(\omega_{n},\varphi_{n})>-\infty$ for any $\omega_{i}\in\Amp(X)$ and $\varphi_{i}\in\mathcal{E}^{1}(\omega_{i})$.
L241: 
L242: For a general bounded-above function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ we set
L243:  | $$\en_{\omega}(\varphi):=\sup\{\en_{\omega}(\psi)\mid\psi\in\PSH(\omega),\psi\leq\varphi\}.$$  |
L244: 
L245: Then $\en_{\omega}(\varphi)=\en_{\omega}(\env_{\omega}(\varphi))$ for any bounded-above function $\varphi$.
L246: A function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{lin}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is said to be of finite energy if it is of the form $\varphi=\varphi^{+}-\varphi^{-}$, where $\varphi^{\pm}\in\mathcal{E}^{1}(\omega)$ for some $\omega\in\Amp(X)$. The energy pairing then extends as a (finite) multilinear pairing $(\theta_{0},\varphi_{0})\cdot\ldots\cdot(\theta_{n},\varphi_{n})$ for arbitrary numerical classes $\theta_{i}\in\Num(X)$ and functions $\varphi_{i}$ of finite energy.
L247: ## 2. Theorem A
L248: 
L249: We now prove Theorem A and derive some consequences.
L250: ### 2.1. Proof of Theorem A
L251: The result is trivial if $\theta$ is not pseudoeffective, as $\PSH(\theta)$ is then empty. Otherwise, we can write $\theta=\lim_{i}c_{1}(L_{i})$ for a sequence of big $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundles $L_{i}$ with $c_{1}(L_{i})\geq\theta$; by [【17†BJ22a】, Lemma 5.9], we may thus assume that $\theta=c_{1}(L)$ for a big $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $L$. Pick $\varphi\in\PL(X)$. By Lemma 1.3, we need to show that $\env_{L}(\varphi)$ is $L$-psh.
L252: By [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 2.31], we have $\varphi=\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}$ for some integrally closed test configuration $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ for $(X,L)$. After replacing $L$ with a multiple, we may further assume that $L$ and $\mathcal{L}$ are honest line bundles.
L253: Since we assume that $\charac k=0$ or $\dim X\leq 2$ (and hence $\dim\mathcal{X}\leq 3$), we can rely on resolution of singularities and assume that $\mathcal{X}$ is smooth and $\mathcal{X}_{0}$ has simple normal crossings support. Assume first that $\charac k=0$, and let $\mathfrak{b}_{m}$ be the multiplier ideal of the graded sequence $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}^{m}$, see Lemma 【25†1.6】.
L254: The inclusion $\mathfrak{a}_{m}\subset\mathfrak{b}_{m}$ is elementary, and we have $\mathfrak{b}_{ml}\subset\mathfrak{b}_{m}^{l}$ for all $m,l$ by the subadditivity property of multiplier ideals. This implies that
L255:  | $$(ml)^{-1}\varphi_{\mathfrak{a}_{ml}}\leq(ml)^{-1}\varphi_{\mathfrak{b}_{ml}}\leq m^{-1}\varphi_{\mathfrak{b}_{m}}$$  |
L256: 
L257: for all $m$ and $l$. Letting $l\to\infty$ shows that
L258: 
L259: (2.1)  |  | $$\varphi_{m}\leq\qq_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})\leq\psi_{m}:=\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}+m^{-1}\varphi_{\mathfrak{b}_{m}}$$  |
L260: for all $m$, by Lemma 【25†1.6】. By the uniform global generation property of multiplier ideals, we can find a $\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}$-equivariant ample line bundle $\mathcal{A}$ on $\mathcal{X}$ such that $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}(m\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{A})\otimes\mathfrak{b}_{m}$ is globally generated for all $m$.
L261: As noted before Lemma 【25†1.6】, this implies $\varphi_{m\mathcal{L}+\mathcal{A}}+\varphi_{\mathfrak{b}_{m}}\in\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}(mL+A)$, with $A\in\Pic(X)$ the restriction of $\mathcal{A}$, and hence
L262:  | $$\psi^{\prime}_{m}:=\psi_{m}+\tfrac{1}{m}\varphi_{\mathcal{A}}\in\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb{Q}}(L+\tfrac{1}{m}A).$$  |
L263: 
L264: After adding to $\mathcal{A}$ a multiple of $\mathcal{X}_{0}$, we may further assume $\varphi_{\mathcal{A}}\geq 0$, which guarantees that the net $(\psi^{\prime}_{m})$ is decreasing with respect to the divisibility order, and hence that $\psi:=\inf_{m}\psi^{\prime}_{m}$ is either $L$-psh or identically $-\infty$ (see [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 4.5]). By (【28†2.1】), we have
L265:  | $$\qq_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})\leq\psi^{\prime}_{m}\leq\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}+\tfrac{1}{m}\varphi_{\mathcal{A}},$$  |
L266: and hence $\qq_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})\leq\psi\leq\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}$. In particular, $\psi\not\equiv-\infty$, so $\psi\in\PSH(L)$, and hence $\psi\leq\env_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})$. Finally, pick $\tau\in\PSH(L)$ such that $\tau\leq\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}$. By Lemma 【29†1.5】, we have $\tau\leq\env_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})=\qq_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})\leq\psi$ on a Zariski open subset of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and hence on $X^{\mathrm{div}}$.
L267: Since $\tau$ and $\psi$ are $L$-psh, it follows from [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 4.22] that $\tau\leq\psi$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$. Taking the sup over $\tau$ yields $\env_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})\leq\psi$, and we conclude, as desired, that $\env_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})=\psi$ is $L$-psh.

L269: ### 2.2. Consequences
L270: 
L271: We now list some consequences of Theorem A. First, we can characterize psef classes, similarly to the complex analytic case.
L272: 
L273: ###### Corollary 2.1.
L274: 
L275: Assume that $X$ satisfies the assumptions in Theorem A. Then, for any $\theta\in\Num(X)$, we have $\PSH(\theta)\neq\emptyset$ iff $\theta$ is psef. Moreover, in this case, the function
L276: 
L277:  | $$V_{\theta}:=\pp_{\theta}(0)$$  |
L278: 
L279: is $\theta$-psh.
L280: ###### Proof.
L281: 
L282: It follows from [【17†BJ22a】, Definition 4.1] that $\PSH(\theta)\neq\emptyset$ only if $\theta$ is psef. First suppose $\theta$ is big. By Theorem A, $V_{\theta}:=\pp_{\theta}(0)$ is $\theta$-psh. Note that $V_{\theta}(v_{\mathrm{triv}})=\sup V_{\theta}=0$, where $v_{\mathrm{triv}}$ is the trivial valuation on $X$.
L283: Now suppose $\theta$ is merely psef, and pick a sequence $(\theta_{m})_{1}^{\infty}$ of big classes converging to $\theta$, such that $\theta\leq\theta_{m+1}\leq\theta_{m}$ for all $m$. As $\PSH(\theta_{m+1})\subset\PSH(\theta_{m})$ for all $m$, the sequence $(V_{\theta_{m}})_{m}$ is pointwise decreasing on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$. Let $\varphi$ be its limit. We have $\sup\varphi=\varphi(v_{\mathrm{triv}})=0$, and $\varphi\in\PSH(\theta_{m})$ for every $m$.
L284: It now follows from [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 4.5] that $\varphi\in\PSH(\theta)$. Finally, it is easy to see that $\varphi=\pp_{\theta}(0)$. Indeed, $\varphi\leq 0$, and if $\psi\in\PSH(\theta)$ satisfies $\psi\leq 0$, then $\psi\in\PSH(\theta_{m})$ for all $m$, so $\psi\leq V_{\theta_{m}}$, and hence $\psi\leq\varphi$. ∎
L285: By [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 5.11], Theorem A now implies the following compactness result.
L286: ###### Corollary 2.2.
L287: 
L288: Under the assumptions on $X$ of Theorem A, the set
L289: 
L290:  | $$\PSH_{\sup}(\theta)=\left\{\varphi\in\PSH(\theta)\mid\sup\varphi=0\right\}$$  |
L291: 
L292: is compact for any psef class $\theta\in\Num(X)$.
L293: 
L294: Finally, as an immediate consequence of Theorem A and [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 6.31], we have the following version of Siu’s decomposition theorem.

L124: Finally, we prove (iii)$\Rightarrow$(i), following [【21†BE21】, Lemma 7.30]. Let $(\varphi_{i})$ be a bounded-above family in $\PSH(\theta)$, and set $\varphi:=\mathrm{sup}^{\star}_{i}\varphi_{i}$. Since $\varphi$ is usc and $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ is compact, we can find a decreasing net $(\psi_{j})$ in $\Cz(X)$ such that $\psi_{j}\to\varphi$.
L125: By density of $\PL(X)$ in $\Cz(X)$ wrt uniform convergence (see [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 2.2]), we can in fact assume $\psi_{j}\in\PL(X)$, and hence $\env_{\theta}(\psi_{j})\in\PSH(\theta)$, by (iii). For all $i,j$, we have $\varphi_{i}\leq\psi_{j}$, and hence $\varphi_{i}\leq\env_{\theta}(\psi_{j})$, which in turn yields $\varphi\leq\env_{\theta}(\psi_{j})\leq\psi_{j}$.
L126: We have thus written $\varphi$ as the limit of the decreasing net of $\theta$-psh functions $\env_{\theta}(\psi_{j})$, which shows that $\varphi$ is $\theta$-psh. ∎
L127: ###### Corollary 1.4.
L128: 
L129: Assume that $\theta$ has the envelope property, and consider a usc function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$. Then:
L130: 
L131:   * (i)
L132: 
L133: $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$ is $\theta$-psh, or $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)\equiv-\infty$;
L134: 
L135:   * (ii)
L136: 
L137: if $\varphi$ is the limit of a decreasing net $(\varphi_{j})$ of bounded-above, usc functions, then $\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})\searrow\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$.
L138: ###### Proof.
L139: 
L140: By Lemma 【22†1.3】, either $\psi:=\env_{\theta}(\varphi)^{\star}$ is $\theta$-psh, or $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)\equiv-\infty$ (the latter being automatic if $\PSH(\theta)=\emptyset$). Since $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)\leq\varphi$ and $\varphi$ is usc, we also have $\psi\leq\varphi$. If $\psi$ is $\theta$-psh, then $\psi\leq\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$, which proves (i).
L141: To see (ii), note that $\rho:=\lim_{j}\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})$ satisfies either $\rho\in\PSH(\theta)$ or $\rho\equiv-\infty$, by [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 4.7]. Furthermore, $\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})\leq\varphi_{j}$ yields, in the limit, $\rho\leq\varphi$, and hence $\rho\leq\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$ (by definition of $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$ if $\rho\in\PSH(\theta)$, and trivially if $\rho\equiv-\infty$). Thus $\lim_{j}\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})=\rho\leq\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$.
L142: On the other hand, $\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})\geq\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$ implies $\rho\geq\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$, which completes the proof of (ii). ∎
L143: ### 1.2. The Fubini–Study envelope
L144: 
L145: Now consider a big $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $L$. Recall [【17†BJ22a】, §2.4] that for any subgroup $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$, $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\Lambda}(L)$ denotes the set of functions $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}$ of the form
L146: 
L147:  | $$\varphi=m^{-1}\max_{j}\{\log|s_{j}|+\lambda_{j}\},$$  |
L148: where $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ is such that $mL$ is an honest line bundle, $(s_{j})_{j}$ is a finite set of nonzero global sections of $mL$, and $\lambda_{j}\in\Lambda$.
L149: 
L150: We define the Fubini–Study envelope of a bounded function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}$ as
L151: 
L152: (1.1)  |  | $$\qq_{L}(\varphi):=\sup\left\{\psi\in\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb{R}}(L)\mid\psi\leq\varphi\right\}.$$  |
L153: By approximation, $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb{R}}(L)$ can be replaced by $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb{Q}}(L)=\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb{Z}}(L)$ in this definition, see [【17†BJ22a】, (2.10)]. Note also that $\qq_{L}(\varphi)\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ is bounded above and lsc.
L154: 
L155: Recall that the augmented base locus of $L$ can be described as
L156:  | $$\mathbb{B}_{+}(L):=\bigcap\{\supp E\mid E\text{ effective }\mathbb{Q}\text{-Cartier divisor},\,L-E\text{ ample}\},$$  |
L157: 
L158: a strict Zariski closed subset of $X$, see [【23†ELMNP06】].
L159: ###### Lemma 1.5.
L160: 
L161: Suppose $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is bounded, with lsc regularization $\varphi_{\star}\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}$. Then $\qq_{L}(\varphi)=\qq_{L}(\varphi_{\star})\leq\env_{L}(\varphi_{\star})$, and equality holds outside $\mathbb{B}_{+}(L)$.
L162: 
L163: In particular, $\qq_{L}(\varphi)=\env_{L}(\varphi_{\star})$ when $L$ is ample. In this case, $\qq_{L}$ coincides with the envelope $\qq_{c_{1}(L)}$ in [【17†BJ22a】, §5.3].
L164: ###### Proof.
L165: Since any function $\psi\in\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}(L)$ is continuous, it satisfies $\psi\leq\varphi$ iff $\psi\leq\varphi_{\star}$. Thus $\qq_{L}(\varphi)=\qq_{L}(\varphi_{\star})$, and we may therefore assume wlog that $\varphi$ is lsc. Since $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}(L)\subset\PSH(L)$, we trivially have $\qq_{L}(\varphi)\leq\env_{L}(\varphi)$. Conversely, pick $\psi\in\PSH(L)$ such that $\psi\leq\varphi$. Let $E$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor such that $A:=L-E$ is ample.

L179: ### 1.3. Envelopes from test configurations
L180: 
L181: Let $L$ be a big line bundle. Any test configuration $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ for $(X,L)$ defines a function $\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}\in\PL$, and we seek to compute the Fubini–Study envelope $\qq_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})$.
L182: To this end, we introduce a slight generalization of the definitions in [【17†BJ22a】, §2.1]. To any $\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}$-invariant ideal $\mathfrak{a}\subset\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}$, we attach a function $\varphi_{\mathfrak{a}}\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to[-\infty,0]$ by setting $\varphi_{\mathfrak{a}}(v):=-\sigma(v)(\mathfrak{a})$, where $\sigma=\sigma_{\mathcal{X}}$ denotes Gauss extension (see [【17†BJ22a】, Remark 1.9]).
L183: In terms of the weight decomposition $\mathfrak{a}=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}}\mathfrak{a}_{\lambda}\varpi^{-\lambda}$ with $\mathfrak{a}_{\lambda}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$, we have $\varphi_{\mathfrak{a}}=\max_{\lambda}\{\log|\mathfrak{a}_{\lambda}|+\lambda\}$.
L184: If $\mathcal{L}$ is an honest line bundle such that $\mathcal{L}\otimes\mathfrak{a}$ is globally generated, one easily checks as in [【17†BJ22a】, Proposition 2.25] that $\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}+\varphi_{\mathfrak{a}}$ lies in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb{Q}}(L)$.
L185: ###### Lemma 1.6.
L186: Let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$, and $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ an integrally closed test configuration for $(X,L)$. For each sufficiently divisible $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, denote by $\mathfrak{a}_{m}\subset\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}$ the base ideal of $m\mathcal{L}$, and set $\varphi_{m}:=\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}+m^{-1}\varphi_{\mathfrak{a}_{m}}$.
L187: Then $\varphi_{m}\in\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{gf}}_{\mathbb{Q}}(L)$ and $(\varphi_{m})_{m}$ forms an increasing net of functions on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ converging pointwise to $\qq_{L}(\varphi_{\mathcal{L}})$.
L188: Here we consider $(\varphi_{m})_{m}$ as a net indexed by the set $m_{0}\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ for some sufficiently divisible $m_{0}$, and partially ordered by divisibility.
L189: 
L190: To prove the lemma, recall [【17†BJ22a】, §1.2] that if $\mathcal{L}$ (and hence $L$) is an honest line bundle, then $\Hnot(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ lies as a $k[\varpi]$-submodule of $\Hnot(X,L)_{k[\varpi^{\pm 1}]}$. The next result provides a valuative characterization of this submodule in terms of $\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}$.
L191: ###### Lemma 1.7.
L192: 
L193: Assume $\mathcal{L}$ is an honest line bundle, pick $s\in\Hnot(X,L)_{k[\varpi^{-\pm 1}]}$, and write $s=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}}s_{\lambda}\varpi^{-\lambda}$ with $s_{\lambda}\in\Hnot(X,L)$. Then $s\in\Hnot(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ iff $\max_{\lambda}\{\log|s_{\lambda}|+\lambda\}\leq\varphi_{\mathcal{L}}$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$.
L194: ###### Proof.
L195: 
L196: By $\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}$-invariance, we have $s\in\Hnot(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})\Leftrightarrow s_{\lambda}\varpi^{-\lambda}\in\Hnot(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{L})$ for all $\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}$, and we may thus assume $s=s_{\lambda}\varpi^{-\lambda}$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}$.
